points: Reports suggest Q2 2026 revenue was $16.1 billion, above the $14.4 billion consensus, so the Q3 print will show whether that demand strength carried into the September quarter and Q4 guidance.

The report will reveal how AI server demand and the 18A ramp are translating into Data Center and AI revenue and margin; that is the main driver of the +39.3% 90-day revenue estimate revision and the 32-to-1 upward analyst revision skew.

Intel Foundry's operating-loss trajectory is a key read; the print should show losses continuing to narrow from the 2023 levels, because Products operating income alone cannot deliver the FY1/FY2 EPS inflection if foundry drag worsens.

Management's Q3/Q4 commentary on capital intensity and supply constraints will matter after Q2 reports flagged rising CapEx and bottlenecks; the long side needs those pressures to stay manageable rather than derail the strong Q3 outlook.

The FY1/FY2 EPS path — from a trailing loss of $2.66 to $1.51 and then $2.04, with 34.8% year-two growth — is the core case; the print must keep that trajectory intact to justify the 0.23x PEG valuation discount to the theme.

AMD and Vertiv report after Intel, so Intel's Q3 results and forward guidance will be the first read on whether AI/data-center capex demand is still accelerating across the active electrical-industry theme.
watch: Q3 revenue and EPS beat the upwardly revised consensus and Q4/FY1 guidance is raised or maintained — supports the long.
Intel Foundry operating loss narrows sequentially and year over year — supports the long.
Data Center and AI revenue grows sequentially — supports the long.
FY1/FY2 EPS guidance stays at or above $1.51 / $2.04 — supports the long.
